subject: Unexpected P99 excursion on streaming endpoints — immediate actions & product questions
messages:
From: Redwood Monitoring <monitoring@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] P99 latency spike on /v1/streaming/generate (zone us-west-2)

Automated alert: from 09:07 -> 09:12 we observed a sustained P99 increase from ~170ms -> 2.3s on the streaming generate endpoint for models running on the 'fastpath' profile in us-west-2. Error rates are low (0.2%) but tail latency has increased across multi-tenant hosts serving FlowMart traffic.

Quick telemetry highlights (attached): p99_latency_topology.png, kv_cache_eviction_log.txt.

Immediate indicators:
- Persistent KV cache miss storms on a subset of shards (eviction flurries at 09:05:30).
- Increased scheduler queue depth on host pool gpu-fp-14.
- No config rollouts in the 2 hours prior.

Recommended immediate triage group: SRE (Ben), Runtime (Soojin), Product (Jonas), CS escalation (Evelyn).

-- Redwood Monitoring
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] P99 latency spike on /v1/streaming/generate (zone us-west-2)

Thanks — looking at hosts now. Short summary of findings so far:
- A subset of keys experienced synchronous cache invalidations after a rare prefix-collision during a shard reshard event; nodes attempted to rebuild large KV segments which serialized forward passes and bloated queue times.
- Host-level CPU on gpu-fp-14 up ~25% vs baseline, but GPU utilization remains normal.

Immediate tactical mitigations I can run in the next 20m:
1) Toggle conservative KV eviction on the affected pool (will reduce miss storms but increases mem usage); requires product ok.
2) Rotate a small fraction (10%) of FlowMart traffic to the backup pool (gpu-fp-20) as a short-term circuit breaker (routing change, ~5m to propagate).
3) Enable request-level soft-timeout to shed particularly large prefix-rebuild requests for 30m.

Questions for Product / Roadmap (Jonas / Karthik):
- Are we OK to flip conservative eviction for the account temporarily? What's the permissible memory headroom for dedicated pools? (product/finance constraints)
- Should we expedite the 'atomic-kv-replay' fix (reduces serialization during reshard) onto the near-term patch train? That is currently scheduled for next quarter.

I can take #1 + #2 now if we get a go. Also collecting heap snapshot/kv logs (attached).

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: heap_snapshot-07-12.tgz
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] P99 latency spike on /v1/streaming/generate (zone us-west-2)

Agree we need a quick customer-safe path. Decisions:
- Approve toggle of conservative KV eviction for the FlowMart-serving pool for up to 4 hours. Ben: please annotate change with rollback tag and metric watch (p99, mem).
- Proceed with rotating 15% of FlowMart traffic to gpu-fp-20 as immediate relief. Soojin: please coordinate routing and confirm no model-variant incompatibility.
- Run soft-timeout (750ms soft) for new streaming requests hitting the affected pool. Product note: this is a customer-visible degradation (trimming tails); CS message required.

Product / Roadmap asks (to Karthik and Soojin):
- Can we create a short-lived patch to the runtime to make prefix rebuilds incremental (reduce serialization)? If not, can we reprioritize 'atomic-kv-replay' to the next biweekly ship? This incident suggests that the ticket should be moved up.
- For the longer term: evaluate a cross-shard prefix-coordination that avoids full-segment invalidation (architectural ask). Estimate required engineering effort (S, M, L).

Evelyn, please prepare a short customer note to FlowMart (draft below). After Ben confirms the toggle + rotation are live and metrics look stable, send to FlowMart ops and Lia.

Jonas Weber
VP Product, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Lia Choi <lia.choi@flowmart.ai>, ops@flowmart.ai
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T12:58:00-07:00
Subject: FlowMart — brief on recent latency tail and next steps (draft)

Hi Lia / FlowMart team,

Wanted to reach out with a quick update following the tail-latency spike you may have observed this morning on streaming responses. Our SRE and runtime teams traced the root cause to a rare KV cache invalidation pattern after a shard reconfiguration that, when combined with certain request prefixes, caused localized serialization of cache rebuilds and higher than normal P99 latency.

What we did right away:
- Enabled a conservative KV eviction tuning for the affected hosts to stop the miss-storm behavior (temporary, will revert within 4 hours pending metrics).
- Rerouted ~15% of your traffic to a warm standby host pool to reduce pressure on the impacted hosts.
- Applied a soft timeout to long-running streaming requests to prevent tail requests from impacting downstream throughput.

What we’re doing next:
- We will monitor the P50/P95/P99 closely and revert the temporary mitigations automatically if we see regression.
- Our engineering team is moving the incremental prefix-rebuild patch up in priority; we’ll share a timeline in the next 48 hours.
- We’ve opened JIRA-RW-9876 to track follow-ups and will include your team on the ticket.

If you saw any customer-facing impact (errors or truncated responses) please let us know — we’re ready to prioritize root-cause follow-ups.

Thanks for the patience — we’ll keep this brief and circle back in 2 hours with metrics.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
